title: A stale runtime store REGENERATES the on-disk extract from its stale contents, silently reverting committed corrections -- three times to one file -- and the revert re-creates the view-skew that blocks the sync which would refresh the store
body:
**THE DESTRUCTIVE PATH NEEDS NO BUG. It is `intent sync --to-disk` -- a documented, correctly-behaving command -- whose SOURCE is a runtime store that may be stale.** There are THREE artefacts in play, not two: **committed canon (`intent/.canon/st/*.json`), the runtime store (`intent/.cache/intent.db`), and the on-disk extract (`intent/st/*/info.md`).** An edit made to canon does not reach the store; `--to-disk` then writes the extract from the STORE, reports success, and silently replaces corrected prose with the stale version. `intent doctor` warns that *"commands are answering from the store and will report the stale model until it is refreshed"* -- **"report" badly understates it: the stale model gets WRITTEN OVER committed corrections.**

Measured on Lamplight, 2026-09-05:

```
git show HEAD:intent/.canon/st/ST0356.json     "_inbox" x1   the CORRECTED text, committed
intent/st/ST0356/info.md            on disk    "_inbox" x4   the STALE text, written back
git status                                     M intent/st/ST0356/info.md
```

**This happened three times to the same file**, each time after the owning node committed the fix. The 1 remaining occurrence in canon is a deliberate historical line that the correction kept, so the count is `3 removed, 1 kept` -- **not a null result, and its survival is the control on the edit itself.**

**Why it is a data-loss shape rather than a nuisance.** A derived cache that misreports is self-correcting the moment anyone reads the source. **A derived cache that WRITES source-of-truth-adjacent artefacts destroys work.** The correction here survived only because it had been committed and could be diffed back. **An uncommitted correction in the same position is gone, with no error, no prompt, and a file that looks untouched apart from its content.**

**And the revert re-creates the finding that blocks other nodes.** The reverted extract produces the `view-skew` that refuses `intent sync --to-store` for a DIFFERENT node's thread (issue `0259`). So the stale store manufactures the blockage, and the blockage prevents the refresh that would fix the stale store.

## The corrected mechanism, and one confusion it explains

A node editing `intent/.canon/st/ST0356.json` directly, then running `--to-disk`, saw the extract NOT change and concluded *"`--to-disk` does not regenerate prose"* -- and wrote that into a commit message, citing the command's own output (*"prose, shipped content and wip/restart are not modelled and are unchanged"*). **That conclusion is wrong and the output line is misleading.** `--to-disk` demonstrably overwrites prose inside an extract; what it had actually done was write the STORE's stale prose, which happened to equal what was already on disk. **Reasoning with two artefacts where there are three produces exactly this: a real write that looks like a no-op.**

## Candidate triggers: one ruled out, one still standing

**RULED OUT, with a positive control: a write scoped to one thread does NOT regenerate another thread's extract.** The first attempt at this test was vacuous -- the divergence had already been removed, so a regenerator that writes only on change had nothing to do, and silence could not distinguish "never writes" from "writes only on difference". Re-run with divergence deliberately arranged:

```
SETUP    extract diverged with a probe marker; store confirmed to lack it
TEST     intent at edit <OTHER-THREAD> ...   extract mtime moved: NO   marker survived: YES
CONTROL  intent sync --to-disk <THREAD>      extract mtime moved: YES  marker overwritten: YES
```

**The control fires, so the test's silence is a real negative.** Restored afterwards; `cmp` against `git show HEAD:` identical.

**STILL STANDING (dc), offered as an untested prediction and labelled as one: the exposure is a store copy that DIVERGED because it was authored outside the sync path.** Where prose had to be hand-written into the store -- there is no CLI verb for it -- the store and the extract are two independently authored texts that can disagree, and a regeneration writes the stale one over the good one. A thread whose store was made a copy of its extract by `--to-store` has nothing stale to write back, so the same regeneration is a no-op for it and destructive for the other. Two points as of filing, verified with `git status` and `git show HEAD:` only. **Falsification: if a thread reconciled through `--to-store` ever reverts, this is wrong.**

**ATTRIBUTION BY TIMING IS NOT RELIABLE HERE AND THE FILING DOES NOT ATTEMPT IT.** Four sessions share that checkout. A write ten seconds before one node's commit reads as that node's doing on that node's terminal and need not be. The trigger is best recorded as **a store-sourced extract regeneration from any node**, not as a named command.

## Two traps for whoever measures this next

**A count over a thread with no extract on disk returns a clean zero that looks exactly like a passing control.** One estate thread has no `info.md` at all; a "control" reading it reports `0` and is vacuous. Confirm the file exists before treating its count as evidence.

**A "did not move" result on a file that already agrees with its source proves nothing.** Arrange the divergence first, and prove with a positive control that the effect CAN be observed, before letting silence mean anything.

## What is wanted

**No command should write an extract from a store the tool knows is stale.** `doctor` already detects the condition, so the check exists and is simply not consulted before the write. Refusing, or regenerating from committed canon instead, would both be correct.

**And the warning text should say what actually happens.** *"Will report the stale model"* tells a reader to distrust output. It does not tell them their committed files are being overwritten, which is the behaviour that costs work.

Reported by Lamplight's `vc` node; found, refined and self-refuted by Lamplight's `ic`, whose file it is, with the standing prediction from `dc`. All measurements taken against `git show HEAD:` rather than through any `intent` command. Related: `0259`, `0256`. The `reporter` field in this register reads `Matthew Sinclair` on every row regardless of origin.
